title: cc connect <service-id> [--check] --json
description: Writes locally-supplied secret VALUES (read exclusively from stdin, never argv/env/a file -- see cc.commands.connect's module docstring) into the per-user OS keychain for one service's missing credential NAMES, then re-runs `cc connections`' own presence checks and returns the fresh row (WP-395 D-6, the manual keychain floor; Task Copilot task 222). `--check` re-evaluates and returns the row only, with no stdin read and no write. Computed entirely CLI-side (invariant #1): this verb reuses `cc connections`' own service-roster/presence-check machinery rather than recomputing what a service requires or what is missing; the only new computation is validating and writing supplied VALUES, which are never echoed anywhere in this payload. See docs/01-architecture/cli-contract.md and claude-copilot/tools/cc/src/cc/commands/connect.py's module docstring for the full design (WP-395/396/398, task 222).

result.description: Envelope-level outcome. 'ok'/'copilot-unavailable'/'org-config-unavailable' carry `cc connections --json`'s own meaning for those values (see connections.schema.json) -- this verb reuses that report internally and passes its envelope-level result straight through when nothing about the input itself was invalid. 'unknown-service': the given service-id/name matched no row in this Mac's roster (`service` is null). 'invalid-input': stdin (in connect mode, when at least one credential was missing) was not valid JSON, or was valid JSON that was not an object of `{"NAME": "value"}` -- `service` is still populated (the row was already resolved before stdin was read) and every requested `credentials[]` entry for a missing name reads `outcome: "failed"` with a plain-language `detail`, never a copy of the malformed input.

detail.description: Plain-language reason, present whenever `result` is not "ok"; null when `result` is "ok". Never a raw passthrough of stdin or an underlying command's stderr (mirrors connections.schema.json's own `store.detail` rule).

mode.description: 'connect': the default -- stdin was read (only when at least one credential name was missing) and any supplied values were written. 'check': `--check` was passed -- read-only re-evaluation, `credentials` is always null.

service.description: The matched service's connections row -- byte-identical shape to `cc connections --json`'s own `connections[]` items (re-evaluated AFTER any writes in connect mode, so `secret_state`/`missing` reflect the outcome). Null when `result` is "unknown-service" or "copilot-unavailable" (no row could be resolved at all).

credentials.description: Null in `check` mode, or when `result` is "unknown-service"/"copilot-unavailable" (nothing was evaluated per-credential). Otherwise one entry per the row's `requires_secret`, in that declared order: a name NOT in the row's `missing` list (as evaluated before this run) reads `already-present` and is never touched, regardless of whether stdin happened to supply a value for it; a name that WAS missing reads `stored` (write succeeded), `already-present` (a race: the keychain already held it by the time this run tried to write it -- never overwritten), or `failed` (no/invalid value supplied, or the keychain write itself failed) -- `detail` on a `failed` entry is always a plain-language reason, NEVER the value or any substring of it. Can be a non-empty array even when `result` is "ok" -- a partial per-credential failure does not change the envelope-level result, by design (mirrors connections.schema.json's own separation of envelope diagnostics from per-row state); a consumer that needs a single success/failure signal should check whether any entry's `outcome` is "failed".

name.description: The credential NAME this outcome is for. Never a value.

outcome.description: 'stored': this run wrote a new value to the OS keychain. 'already-present': nothing needed writing (see `credentials`' own description for the two cases this covers). 'failed': no value was written -- see `detail`.

detail.description: Plain-language reason for a `failed` outcome (e.g. "value must not be empty.", "no value was provided for this credential."); null for `stored`/`already-present`. NEVER contains the credential value or any substring of it.
